messages:
maya: Heads-up — AcmeCorp just filed a ticket: calls to /v1/generate are returning 401 invalid_api_key across multiple hosts. They rotated keys yesterday and started seeing this ~10:12 UTC. Req id they sent: req_0a1b2c.

ben: thanks. do we have the raw curl they used? headers?

maya: pasted from customer support convo:
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-0a2b3c\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}'
```
Response: 401
```
{\n  "error": {\n    "type": "invalid_api_key",\n    "message": "API key is invalid or expired."\n  }\n}
```

ricardo: did they copy/paste from an email or CLI? trailing newline or extra chars can break the header. also confirm the key prefix is correct: sk- vs rk- etc.

maya: they say they used the SDK too and got same 401. account id: acct_acme_42.

support-bot: Note: key rotation event for acct_acme_42 recorded at 2024-11-14T10:05:12Z (rotation-triggered-by: user).

ben: ok that matches. rotation happened ~7 minutes before error spike. possible we disabled old key and customer kept using it. can someone check key status?

devops-oncall: running quick lookup against key metadata.
```
# internal admin CLI (redwoodctl)
redwoodctl keys get sk-live-0a2b3c --account acct_acme_42
```
Result: status: disabled, revoked_at: 2024-11-14T10:05:12Z, reason: manual-rotation

ricardo: so the key was revoked at rotation time. two likely causes: (1) customer didn't update client to new key, or (2) rotation script left DNS/CI with old secret. advise customer to deploy new secret and confirm no env var caching.

maya: customer says they redeployed services but still 401. they pasted logs showing Authorization header present. here's excerpt (redacted):
```
[2024-11-14T10:18:03Z] request id=req_0a1b2c headers={Authorization: "Bearer sk-live-0a2b3c\n", Host: "api.redwood.ai"}
```
Looks like a newline got appended when reading from file.

ben: aha — trailing newline in header value will cause signature mismatch / token lookup to fail and be treated as invalid. our header parser doesn't trim.

ricardo: quick mitigation: ask them to trim whitespace when reading secret or set env var without newline. Example in bash: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /secrets/acme-key | tr -d '\n')`

maya: passed mitigation to customer. also suggested to regenerate new key so they can rotate cleanly.

customer (via maya): regenerated key and did `echo -n` check — still 401 when using new key from CI only. works locally though.

ben: hmm, if it works locally but not in CI, suspect the CI runner injects secrets with CRLF or adds quotes. can they print hex of first 12 bytes of key in CI (redact output) to confirm? e.g. `printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | xxd -l 12`

maya: they ran that and got different output than local. CI shows trailing `0a` byte (newline). new key fixed after changing CI secret injection to raw value. customer confirms success.

support-bot: Incident note appended to acct_acme_42: root_cause=key_revoked + client_env_whitespace. action=reissue_key + advise_ci_fix.

maya: recording internal remediation: we should add a short help blurb in rotation docs: "If using file-based secrets, ensure no trailing newline (use echo -n or tr -d '\\n')." will open a tiny docs PR.

ricardo: also put a one-liner in SDKs to warn on whitespace in API key env var at client init (log warn once). I'll file a ticket.

ben: closing loop with customer now — they confirmed flows back to green. marking thread resolved once PRs are created. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all. follow-ups: DOCS-201 (add rotation tip), SDK-453 (envvar whitespace warning).

devops-oncall: logged runbook note: when 401 invalid_api_key after rotation, check: (1) key status in admin, (2) header whitespace/newlines, (3) key prefix and scope, (4) CI/secret manager injection.

maya: marking resolved, will update ticket. :white_check_mark:
